terms.definition: SDAD is a paradigm shift in the software development lifecycle where AI agents, rather than human developers, serve as the primary builders by ingesting massive Functional Requirement Documents. It leverages frontier models with multi-million token context windows to maintain a holistic understanding of an entire codebase, allowing for the autonomous translation of high-level business specs into integrated production code.
terms.analogy: Imagine a Master Chef who doesn't touch a knife but instead reads a 50-page banquet specification and directs a team of automated sous-chefs to execute every course simultaneously, ensuring the flavor profile of the appetizer perfectly complements the dessert without manual intervention.
terms.business_value: This eliminates the 'translation tax' between business stakeholders and engineers. For the C-suite, this means a drastic reduction in R&D overhead and the ability to pivot product features in days rather than months by treating natural language requirements as the source of truth.

terms.definition: This safety technique moves beyond surface-level 'refusal' filters by probing the internal, hidden layers of a neural network to identify harmful underlying logic before it reaches the output stage. It specifically targets 'semantic camouflage,' where a model might be tricked into providing dangerous information by wrapping it in a benign-sounding context.
terms.analogy: It is like a high-tech airport security scanner that looks past a passenger's polite smile and professional suit to detect a concealed weapon in their luggage before they even reach the boarding gate.
terms.business_value: As enterprises face increasing pressure regarding AI ethics and security, this technology provides a robust 'immune system' for corporate LLMs. It protects brand reputation by preventing sophisticated jailbreaks that traditional, easily bypassed safety filters would miss.

terms.definition: This is a performance optimization for agentic LLMs that decouples the heavy computational cost of loading tool schemas from the active reasoning process. By 'splicing' pre-computed segments of memory (the Key-Value Cache), the system can instantly swap between thousands of external tools and APIs without the latency typically caused by re-processing long system prompts.
terms.analogy: Think of it as a Formula 1 pit crew using pre-mounted tires and pre-measured fuel pods that can be 'spliced' onto the car in seconds, rather than having to manufacture a new set of wheels every time the car enters the pit lane.
terms.business_value: This technology solves the 'Time-to-First-Token' (TTFT) bottleneck, which is the primary killer of user experience in AI agents. For the bottom line, this enables hyper-responsive, complex AI workflows that feel instantaneous to the end-user, even when the AI is navigating vast libraries of enterprise software tools.
